messages:
luis-customer: Hey team — we rotated an API key ~4h ago via the Admin UI. Since then our mobile clients intermittently get 403s when making generate requests. Looks like it happens after app background/foreground or when connections drop. Sample error from our client: `error 403: api_key_invalid`

mia-support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you share the affected customer/org id and which SDK/version you use? Any proxy/edge in front?

luis-customer: Org: org_88XY, app ver 2.4.3, using our custom HTTP client with bearer header `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`. No external proxy, we talk to hosted Redwood in us-west-2. We rotated the key from the Admin UI (rotated old key -> new key and revoked old).

mia-support: Thanks. Quick question — after rotation did you redeploy app or restart any worker processes? Also are you pinning keys in env vars or using a secret-mgmt sidecar?

luis-customer: We rely on Kubernetes env vars (Deployment manifest updated by our CI). CI pushed new secret to Vault then updated k8s secret and did a `kubectl rollout` but we did not restart all pods immediately. Some pods restarted later due to auto-scaler.

raj-engineering: FYI — intermittent 403s after rotation + partial pod restarts usually point at stale in-process caches or sidecars that haven't reloaded the env. If the process keeps the old key in memory, long-lived connections can keep using revoked key.

mia-support: Can you reproduce by forcing a pod reuse? Steps to try quickly: 1) `kubectl exec -it pod-xyz -- curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` 2) restart pod and retry. Also check app logs for `Authorization` header used.

luis-customer: Ran a direct curl from pod A (pre-restart) -> 403. After `kubectl delete pod pod-A` the new pod with updated env returns 200. So confirms pod-level staleness.

raj-engineering: Root cause: key rotation is fine server-side, but our client infra keeps in-process env var cached (no hot-reload) and long-lived keep-alive connections reuse revoked credentials. Also if you're using a sidecar (vault-agent) and the agent didn't reload the process, the application won't pick up new value. Short-term mitigation: force a rolling restart of all app pods.

mia-support: Workaround instructions sent to customer: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/my-app` or trigger CI job to restart. For serverless (lambda) do a config redeploy. Also adding a client-side retry with a refresh-on-403 path helps — on 403 try fetching current key then retry once.

ops-bot: deploy recorded: rotation-hotfix-5115006810 by ci-user.

raj-engineering: Long-term fix options: 1) Add warning in Rotation UI that partial rollout may cause 4xx to clients that haven’t picked up new creds; 2) Encourage using short-lived tokens + KMS/Vault sidecars that emit notifications and signal consumers; 3) Add server-side grace window where revoked keys remain valid for N seconds to allow rolling restarts (opt-in). For Redwood internal docs, add runbook for support on how to handle these escalations.

mia-support: Noted — I'll escalate doc update + add CI checks to advise a full rollout after rotation.

luis-customer: Thanks — rolling restart cleared the errors. One follow-up: any recommended pattern so next rotation is zero-downtime?

raj-engineering: Recommend these patterns: - use dynamic short-lived tokens (rotate transparently) - adopt connection teardown on 403 so clients refresh key - use sidecars that update processes via signal/local socket instead of env-only; or orchestrate rotation with a coordinated rolling restart. We're drafting a KB entry.

mia-support: Closing loop — customer confirmed resolution, we'll track a KB: "API key rotation: pod env churn and in-process cache" and add a UI hint. Marking thread resolved but keeping notes for SRE/Platform to discuss grace-window tradeoffs.

luis-customer: Appreciate the fast help :pray: Will wait for KB and update our deploy pipeline to include restart step after rotation.
